title: Local models of the fibres of a composite
statement: Let $a:U\to X$ and $f:X\to S$ be locally finite type morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $u\in U$, $x=a(u)$, $s=f(x)$. Put $A=\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$, $B=\mathcal O_{U_s,u}$ and $C=\mathcal O_{U_x,u}$, using scheme-theoretic fibres [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and local rings (structure-sheaf stalks [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]). These are Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; the induced map $A\to B$ is local (the inverse image of the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_B$ is $\mathfrak m_A$), its closed fibre is canonically $B/\mathfrak m_A B\cong C$, and it is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] if $a$ is flat at $u$ [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Each of the three pointed fibres admits an affine open neighbourhood of its indicated point that is finite type over its ground field, namely $\kappa(s),\kappa(s),\kappa(x)$ respectively [def-weil-residue-field]. The stalks and residue fields on these neighbourhoods identify with the indicated fibre stalks and with $\kappa(x),\kappa(u),\kappa(u)$ respectively, compatibly with the residue-field tower $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(x)\to\kappa(u)$.

source.place: Tag 0HA1 (lemma-local-ring-fibre); Morphisms Tag 01T3 (lemma-composition-finite-type), Tag 01T4 (lemma-base-change-finite-type), Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), Tag 01U8 (lemma-base-change-module-flat), and Tag 02FX (lemma-dimension-fibre-at-a-point), affine fibre reductions

proof.text: By clause (e) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], $f\circ a$ is locally of finite type. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change] to $f$, $f\circ a$, and $a$, over $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$, $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$, and $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ respectively. Thus $X_s,U_s,U_x$ are locally of finite type over their indicated fields. The universal property in [def-pc-fibre-product] gives the map $a_s:U_s\to X_s$: its projections are $a$ composed with the projection to $U$, and the projection to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$. Its point over $u$ maps to the point over $x$ by [def-pc-scheme-fibre].

For each of these three field schemes, the defining affine cover in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] over the affine base $\operatorname{Spec}k$ supplies an affine neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}E$ of the specified point. By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], $E$ is finitely generated over $k$. Hence $V\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite type: its one affine chart is a finite cover of the preimage of the whole base. A field is Noetherian since each ideal is either zero or generated by $1$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] to get $E$ Noetherian. At the chosen point, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] gives the stalk as $E_{\mathfrak p}$, and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] makes it Noetherian. These are precisely $A,B,C$. They are local because they are stalks of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. This argument never assumes $S,X,U$ themselves Noetherian or globally of finite type.

For a morphism of schemes $g:Y\to T$, a point $y\in Y$ and $t=g(y)$, [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient] says that the stalk map of the first projection $Y_t=Y\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)\to Y$ at the point of $Y_t$ over $y$ is a surjection $\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to\mathcal O_{Y_t,y}$ with kernel $\mathfrak m_t\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, the ideal generated by the image of $\mathfrak m_t$ under $g^\sharp_y$; so it induces $\mathcal O_{Y,y}/\mathfrak m_t\mathcal O_{Y,y}\cong\mathcal O_{Y_t,y}$, sending the class of every germ to its image germ. We use it three times: for $g=f$ at $y=x$ over $t=s$, for $g=f\circ a$ at $y=u$ over $t=s$ (whose stalk map at $u$ is $a^\sharp_u\circ f^\sharp_x$ by the composition rule), and for $g=a$ at $y=u$ over $t=x$. The points of the fibres over $x$ and $u$ are those named in step 1.

Put $R=\mathcal O_{S,s}$, $D=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $E=\mathcal O_{U,u}$ and $I=\mathfrak m_R D$. Apply step 3 to $f,f\circ a,a$. Its projection-compatible isomorphisms give $A=D/I$, $B=E/\mathfrak m_R E$, and $C=E/\mathfrak m_D E$. Since $a_s$ is a scheme morphism, [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism] makes $A\to B$ local. More explicitly, the commuting projection square identifies this map with $d\bmod I\mapsto a_u^\sharp(d)\bmod\mathfrak m_R E$: both composites from $D$ are the same stalk map by the stated composition rule. Because $R\to D$ is local, $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_D$ and $\mathfrak m_A=\mathfrak m_D/I$. Thus $\mathfrak m_A B$ is generated by the classes of $a_u^\sharp(\mathfrak m_D)$, and $B/\mathfrak m_A B\to C$, sending the class of $e$ to $e\bmod\mathfrak m_D E$, is an isomorphism: the map $E\to B/\mathfrak m_A B$ is surjective and its kernel is exactly $\mathfrak m_D E$, since $\mathfrak m_R E\subseteq\mathfrak m_D E$. This is the canonical closed-fibre identification.

source.place: Tag 0HA1 (lemma-local-ring-fibre), applied three times; the double quotient calculation is written out

proof.text: If $a$ is flat at $u$, [def-weil-flat-morphism] says $E$ is a flat $D$-module. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-quotient-flat] with the ideal $I=\mathfrak m_R D$. It says $E/IE$ is flat over $D/I$. The ideal $IE$ equals $\mathfrak m_R E$: its generators are the composites of elements of $\mathfrak m_R$, and extending a generated ideal twice does not change its generators. Hence the quotients from step 4 are $A=D/I$ and $B=E/IE$, with exactly the induced scalar action $d\bmod I$ acting through $a_u^\sharp(d)$. Therefore $A\to B$ is flat. Only flatness at the specified point was used; global flatness of $a$ was not substituted for it.

source.place: Tag 01U8 (lemma-base-change-module-flat), pointwise special case; Algebra Tag 00HI (lemma-flat-base-change) for the quotient-flatness argument

proof.text: The fibre projections preserve the residue fields explicitly. For each application of step 3, the ideal $\mathfrak m_tD$ lies in the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_y$ of $D$ because the original stalk map is local. The quotient $D/\mathfrak m_tD$ has maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_y/\mathfrak m_tD$: elements outside it are classes of units of $D$, while the further quotient is the field $D/\mathfrak m_y$. Its residue field is therefore canonically $D/\mathfrak m_y$ by $[d]\mapsto[d]$. Apply this to the three fibres to obtain $\kappa(x),\kappa(u),\kappa(u)$. On each chosen affine neighbourhood, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identifies the same stalk through the germ map, so quotienting by its unique maximal ideal identifies the same residue field. By [def-weil-residue-field] and the composition rule of [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], the maps of residue fields are obtained by reducing the actual stalk maps. Thus a germ $r\in R$ maps to the class of $f_x^\sharp(r)$ in $\kappa(x)$ and then to the class of $a_u^\sharp f_x^\sharp(r)$ in $\kappa(u)$; this is also its image through the composite. The isomorphisms above send every germ to its own residue class, so commute with these maps and give the asserted tower compatibility.
